info.title: Mailery API
info.description: Mailery API for accounts, API keys, billing, hosted mailboxes, messages, digests, domains, customer webhooks, provider webhooks, and admin operations. All endpoints are versioned under /api/v1; per-endpoint rate limits, the versioning/deprecation policy, and the contract changelog live in docs/API.md and docs/CHANGELOG.md.

minutes.description: Alias for olderThanMinutes. Only flag events older than this many minutes.

olderThanMinutes.description: Only flag events older than this many minutes.

subscriptionLimit.description: Maximum local subscriptions to cross-check against Stripe.

predeploy.description: Also fail when legacy positive credit balances need authoritative reconciliation.

reason.description: Suspension reason recorded on the tenant and audit log. Defaults to operator_freeze.

clearBillingFlag.description: Defaults to true. Pass false to keep billing_flag in place.

tenantId.description: Target tenant. An unknown id is 404 not_found before any replay claim is written.

amount.description: Non-zero integer credit delta: positive grants (source admin), negative debits.

reason.description: Operator reason, recorded on the ledger row and the credit.adjust audit row.

replayed.description: true when this response was replayed from an earlier request carrying the same Idempotency-Key; the ledger was not adjusted again.

AuditPurgeScope.description: What an audit purge touches. Fixed today: every tenant's admin_audit rows past the retention window.

count.description: admin_audit rows the purge would delete (created strictly before cutoff).

cutoff.description: The cutoff the purge would use: now minus retention_months.

apply_token.description: Short-lived HMAC token bound to count, cutoff, scope and the requesting actor. Required by POST /api/v1/admin/audit/purge; single-use.

AuditPurgeApplyRequest.description: Exactly one of applyToken (canonical) or apply_token (the preflight response's own field name) carries the token; when both are sent, applyToken wins.

apply_token.description: Alias for applyToken, matching the preflight response's field name.

removed.description: Rows deleted; always equal to preflight_count (any difference rolls the purge back).

cutoff.description: The cutoff bound into the token, not a fresh one.

apply_token_id.description: The token's id, also recorded on the audit.purge row (after.apply_token_id), which is what makes the token single-use.

shared_domain.description: Shared Mailery-owned sending domain for the Free tier (MAILERY_SHARED_DOMAIN); null when the deployment has none configured.

db.description: Result of a short-deadline database ping.

latency_ms.description: Ping latency; present when ok is true.

error.description: Ping failure reason; present when ok is false.

DomainBoundaryContract.description: Platform domain boundary contract. mailery.co is a system_domain; customer domains are tenant_domain records; external domains outside hosted tenant control use self_hosted_domain records. DMARC gates outbound ramp only and must not block non-sending aggregation.

warmup.description: Pending means warming with available capacity; blocked means paused or daily capacity exhausted.

renewal.description: Renewal tracking (launch lane L07); present on GET /api/v1/domains/{id}. Null for a connected domain.

acceptedTerms.description: Explicit unselected acceptance of the exact termsVersion. Never inferred.

termsVersion.description: Exact SHA-256 version returned by GET /api/v1/terms/current

scopes.description: Tenant-mintable scopes. New keys default to least privilege ['mail_read','mail_write'] when none are specified. 'domains:purchase' gates the irreversible domain-purchase path and must be requested explicitly (or covered by 'full'). 'admin' is not selectable; legacy keys carrying it are aliased to 'full'.

MessageListPage.description: Lightweight, bodyless message page. Excludes text_body, html_body, clean_markdown, raw_email, metadata and classification (see GET /messages/{id}).

next_cursor.description: Full-microsecond (sort_at,id) keyset cursor, or null on the last page.

MessageListItem.description: Bodyless list item. snake_case and camelCase are both emitted; snake_case shown here.

snippet.description: Maintained <=200 char preview; never detoasts the body columns.

is_starred.description: Real star flag, distinct from is_important. Backs the 'starred' folder view.

updated_at.description: Exact per-row change watermark. A GET /messages/changes client advances its watermark from each row's updated_at (also emitted as updatedAt).

MessageChangesPage.description: Delta / JMAP-changesSince page. Same bodyless items as MessageListPage, ordered by updated_at ASC, plus a server-issued watermark.

next_cursor.description: Full-microsecond (updated_at,id) keyset cursor, or null on the last page.

server_time.description: Server clock captured before the read. Also returned as the X-Mailery-Server-Time header. Once fully drained (next_cursor null), a client may adopt this as its next updatedSince watermark.

Label.description: Tenant label with its per-label live-message count. System-label counts come from the O(1) folder counters (message_counters); custom-label counts are computed from message_labels joined to live messages. count is also emitted as message_count / messageCount.

count.description: Number of live (non-deleted) messages for this label: the folder counter for a system label, the message_labels join count for a custom label.

BulkMessageRequest.description: Bounded, tenant-scoped, counter-correct bulk mutation. Provide either an explicit id list OR a { mailboxId, folder } filter, plus an action.

ids.description: Explicit id list (<= 1000). Mutually exclusive with the mailboxId/folder filter.

mailboxId.description: Filter path: scope the action to one mailbox. Alias: mailbox_id.

folder.description: Filter path: restrict to a folder/group. Alias: group.

cursor.description: Resume token (filter path only): pass back a prior next_cursor to continue draining a large folder.

affected.description: Rows that actually transitioned (not merely matched).

has_more.description: Filter path only: true if a resume cursor is returned.

status.description: Current message status. For an outbound message this is the delivery status: queued before the provider dispatch, sent after it, failed once the provider reported a bounce, complaint, rejection or rendering failure, and test_sent on a server that never dispatches (MAILERY_MAIL_MODE != live).

delivery_status.description: Alias of `status`, named for readers that only care about delivery.

last_event_at.description: Provider timestamp of the newest row in this message's delivery timeline (GET /api/v1/messages/{id}/events), or null when no provider feedback has arrived. Never a stand-in such as created_at, so "no feedback yet" stays distinguishable from "delivered".

replayed.description: Only on a POST /messages/send response that carried an Idempotency-Key: true when this response replayed the send already bound to that key rather than sending again.

idempotency_key.description: Only on a POST /messages/send response: the key this result is bound to, when one was supplied.

SendAttachment.description: One attachment. Supply EITHER `content` (base64 of the file) OR `attachmentId` (an attachment already stored on this tenant, e.g. one that arrived inbound); supplying both is a 400. At most 10 attachments and 10 MiB decoded in total per message — the decoded ceiling that keeps the assembled MIME (base64 inflates by 4/3) far inside the provider's 40 MB message limit.

filename.description: Display filename. Defaults to "attachment"; path separators and control characters are stripped.

contentType.description: MIME type, e.g. application/pdf. Defaults to application/octet-stream.

content.description: Base64 file content. Mutually exclusive with attachmentId.

attachmentId.description: Id of an attachment already stored on this tenant. Mutually exclusive with content.

SendRequest.description: A hosted send. The message is assembled as raw RFC 5322 MIME and dispatched through the provider's raw content path, which is what carries attachments, threading headers and the server-generated Message-Id.

mailboxId.description: Mailbox to send from. Must be active and Mailery-managed.

bcc.description: Envelope-only: blind copies are passed to the provider as envelope recipients and never written as a Bcc header, so the visible recipients cannot see them.

html.description: HTML body. With `text` too, the message is sent as multipart/alternative.

replyTo.description: Reply-To addresses, written as a header on the raw message.

inReplyTo.description: Parent Message-ID for a threaded reply (angle brackets optional). The server writes In-Reply-To from it and appends it to References, per RFC 5322 3.6.4.

references.description: The parent's References ancestry, oldest-first, as an array or a raw header value. Capped at 25 ids (thread root plus the most recent).

headers.description: Custom headers, at most 10, each value at most 900 characters. Allowlisted: any `X-` name EXCEPT the reserved `x-ses-`, `x-amz-`, `x-mailery-` and `x-sns-` prefixes, plus the standard filing headers auto-submitted, comments, importance, keywords, list-help, list-id, list-subscribe, list-unsubscribe, list-unsubscribe-post, organization, precedence, priority, sensitivity. Identity, routing and authentication headers (From, Sender, To, Cc, Bcc, Reply-To, Return-Path, Date, Message-ID, In-Reply-To, References, Subject, MIME-Version, Content-*, DKIM-Signature, Received, Authentication-Results) are rejected with 400 header_not_allowed: they are set by Mailery.

idempotencyKey.description: Alternative to the Idempotency-Key header for transports that cannot set headers. The header wins when both are present.

mailboxId.description: Mailbox to send from. Must be active and Mailery-managed.

bcc.description: Envelope-only: blind copies are passed to the provider as envelope recipients and never written as a Bcc header, so the visible recipients cannot see them.

html.description: HTML body. With `text` too, the message is sent as multipart/alternative.

replyTo.description: Reply-To addresses, written as a header on the raw message.

inReplyTo.description: Parent Message-ID for a threaded reply (angle brackets optional). The server writes In-Reply-To from it and appends it to References, per RFC 5322 3.6.4.

references.description: The parent's References ancestry, oldest-first, as an array or a raw header value. Capped at 25 ids (thread root plus the most recent).

headers.description: Custom headers, at most 10, each value at most 900 characters. Allowlisted: any `X-` name EXCEPT the reserved `x-ses-`, `x-amz-`, `x-mailery-` and `x-sns-` prefixes, plus the standard filing headers auto-submitted, comments, importance, keywords, list-help, list-id, list-subscribe, list-unsubscribe, list-unsubscribe-post, organization, precedence, priority, sensitivity. Identity, routing and authentication headers (From, Sender, To, Cc, Bcc, Reply-To, Return-Path, Date, Message-ID, In-Reply-To, References, Subject, MIME-Version, Content-*, DKIM-Signature, Received, Authentication-Results) are rejected with 400 header_not_allowed: they are set by Mailery.

idempotencyKey.description: This message's own stable key. A repeated key replays that message's original result instead of sending it again; the replayed message's meter unit is returned to the batch.

SendBatchMetering.description: How the batch was metered. The meter is drawn ONCE for every message in the batch, before any message is attempted; units are returned afterwards for exactly the messages that never reached the provider.

unit.description: Which meter the batch drew from. `none` on a server with MAILERY_MAIL_MODE != live: nothing dispatches, so nothing is metered.

credits_charged.description: Credits debited up front (0 on the free monthly-allowance path and in non-live mode).

refunded.description: Messages whose unit was returned: they failed strictly before their provider dispatch, or replayed an earlier result.

retained.description: Messages whose unit stays consumed: sent, or failed AFTER their dispatch (the outcome is ambiguous, so the unit is never returned).

index.description: Position in the submitted messages array.

replayed.description: True when this item replayed a result already bound to its idempotency key; no message was sent for it here.

dispatched.description: Whether THIS batch pushed the message to the provider. False after a failure means the meter unit was returned; true after a failure means the outcome is ambiguous and the unit stays consumed.

MessageEvent.description: One provider delivery event on a message's timeline. Recorded from the same provider notification that drives the email.* customer webhooks, so the push and pull surfaces cannot disagree. Metadata only — never message bodies.

type.description: The customer webhook event name without its `email.` prefix.

recipient.description: First recipient the event is about.

reason_code.description: Provider reason, e.g. Permanent/General for a hard bounce or abuse for a complaint.

occurred_at.description: Provider event timestamp (not the row's insert time).

last_event_at.description: Provider timestamp of the newest event, or null when no provider feedback has arrived. Never a stand-in such as created_at.

quoteToken.description: Required when purchase/buy is true. Signed token returned by GET /api/v1/domains/availability.

maxPriceCents.description: Required when purchase/buy is true. Maximum all-in price authorized by the caller.

currency.description: Required when purchase/buy is true. Three-letter authorized quote currency.

address.description: Mailbox local part to create or plan.

autoRenew.description: Domain auto-renew is off by default; opt in explicitly.

quoteToken.description: Signed quote token returned by GET /api/v1/domains/availability.

maxPriceCents.description: Maximum all-in price authorized by the caller in minor units.

currency.description: Three-letter currency authorized by the caller.

DomainPurchaseResult.description: Result of POST /api/v1/domains/purchase. Extends the tenant-domain status envelope with per-step lifecycle progress.

ownership_ready.description: True once ownershipStatus is ready (the PIVOT P5 acceptance).

resumed.description: True when the domain was already registered and this call resumed the lifecycle instead of charging/registering again.

verify_error.description: Present when the verify step failed; the registration is preserved. The same Idempotency-Key exactly replays this stored result; obtain a fresh quote and use a new key to continue the incomplete lifecycle.

DomainProviderStatus.description: Connected domains skip the availability lookup only when the complete tenant-persisted record has purchase_status=not_requested and no paid-attempt provenance. Any retained marker, even malformed, and purchased or unknown/untracked domains retain the check.

check_status.description: An availability lookup was deliberately not requested. available=false and purchase_supported=false are conservative; no quote is returned.

plan.description: Paid identity tier to subscribe to (defaults to 'pro'). The 'free' tier has no checkout.

country.description: Customer-declared ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 billing or residence country. Not nationality or IP.

countryPolicyVersion.description: Exact version read from GET /api/v1/billing/countries after presenting its restrictions to the customer.

CheckoutRequest.description: New purchases require the full country declaration. Omitting all three declaration fields replays only an exact pre-country claim: checkout retains its original actor/kind/plan/credits fingerprint, and wallet retains its original amountCents fingerprint under the authenticated tenant and key. Missing claims fail country admission before insertion or provider I/O. Supplying any declaration never matches a legacy fingerprint. Retain the exact original countryPolicyVersion on retries; never substitute the current version.

password.description: The owner's current password. Password re-authentication is mandatory; a bearer token alone cannot delete the account.

AccountExport.description: GDPR Art. 20 data export. The small collections (tenant, users, mailboxes, labels, api_keys, domains, subscriptions, credits) are complete on every page; messages (with full bodies and attachment metadata) are keyset-paginated on id ASC — walk messages.next_cursor until null and concatenate messages.data. Private warm-up feedback receipts have a separate bounded metadata/count page and next_cursor, including receipts after message deletion. Salt and recipient hashes are never exported.

api_keys.description: API key metadata only; secrets are never exported.

ledger.description: Complete credit transaction history, oldest first.

items.description: Full message rows including rawEmail, textBody, htmlBody, cleanMarkdown, classification, and metadata, plus delivery_events for its retained delivery timeline and attachment metadata with a download_url per attachment (binary content stays behind GET /api/v1/attachments/{id}/download). Includes warmup_attempt for its retained reservation and recipient feedback, or null. Includes inbound_receipt for its retained delivery receipt, or null (35-day retention, survives message deletion).

next_cursor.description: Message-id keyset cursor; null on the last page.

domain_warmup_days.description: Retained daily warm-up counters; message pages also include their warmup_attempt recipient evidence.

inbound_usage_windows.description: Retained UTC monthly inbound usage windows (180 days); credit ledger retains overage debits.

items.description: Original tenant receipt metadata only: id,domain,day,provider_message_id,reserved,delivered,bounced,complained,created_at. No private salts or hashes.

terms_acceptances.description: Owner-path projection of immutable tenant consent receipts. Does not infer consent for old accounts.

withdrawal_evidence.description: Owner-created identified/confirmed withdrawal records with preserved purchase/consent/policy evidence. Independent cursor.

token.description: Signed, short-lived quote token bound to tenant, domain, customer total, currency, and expiry.

WebhookEventType.description: Customer webhook event types. Filters may also use group wildcards (`email.*`, `domain.*`, `billing.*`, `webhook.*`).

WebhookEndpointStatus.description: `disabled` = paused by the customer; `dead` = taken offline by the circuit breaker after 20 consecutive failed deliveries. PATCH status=active re-enables either.

WebhookDeliveryStatus.description: `pending` = not yet attempted; `failed` = last attempt failed, retry scheduled at next_attempt_at; `dead` = retries exhausted (12 attempts), dead-lettered; `delivered` = a 2xx was received.

events.description: Event filter (exact types or group wildcards). null = every event.

secret_prefix.description: First characters of the signing secret (`whsec_` + 6) for identification; the secret itself is only returned on create/rotate.

failure_count.description: Consecutive failed deliveries; reset to 0 by a successful delivery or by PATCH status=active. The breaker trips at 20.

url.description: Absolute https URL on a public host.

events.description: Event filter: entries from WebhookEventType or group wildcards such as `email.*`. Omit or send [] for every event.

secret.description: Plaintext signing secret (`whsec_` + 43 base64url chars). Shown exactly once; store it where the receiver verifies Mailery-Signature.

event_id.description: Shared by every delivery (and redelivery) of the same event; consumers dedupe on it. Sent as Mailery-Event-Id and as body.id.

response_status.description: HTTP status of the last attempt; null when the request never completed (timeout, DNS/SSRF refusal, connection error).

next_attempt_at.description: Scheduled time of the next attempt; null once terminal (delivered or dead).

last_error.description: Redacted, truncated (500 chars) description of the last failure: status line plus a body snippet, or the transport/guard error.

payload.description: The event `data` object exactly as delivered (never message bodies).

WebhookEventEnvelope.description: The JSON body POSTed to a webhook endpoint. Headers: Mailery-Event-Id, Mailery-Event-Type, Mailery-Delivery-Id, Mailery-Delivery-Attempt, Mailery-Timestamp (unix seconds), Mailery-Signature (`v1=` + hex HMAC-SHA256 over `${timestamp}.${rawBody}` with the endpoint secret). Verify over the raw body bytes and reject timestamps outside a 5-minute window. See docs/API.md "Webhooks".

data.description: Event-specific payload. email.received: message_id, mailbox_id, from, to[], subject, received_at, has_attachments. email.sent|delivered|bounced|complained|rejected: message_id, provider_message_id, recipient, recipients[], reason_code, occurred_at. domain.ready|blocked: domain_id, domain, reason, status, send_enabled, inbound_enabled, outbound_status, inbound_status, dmarc_status. billing.suspended: reason, suspended_at, effects[]. webhook.test: endpoint_id, message, requested_at.

SuppressionReason.description: Why the address is suppressed. bounce and complaint are written from provider feedback; manual is an explicit entry.

source.description: Where the entry came from (e.g. ses).

Wallet.description: Prepaid USD wallet (launch lane L07). Integer cents, entirely separate from the send-credit balance: credits meter sends, wallet cents pay for domain purchases and renewals.

balance_cents.description: Spendable balance in USD cents. Never negative.

maximum_topup_cents.description: Largest accepted single top-up; repeat the top-up for a larger balance.

delta_cents.description: Signed cents. Zero only for a `loss` marker row.

source.description: `loss` is a zero-delta marker for refunded funds already spent on a completed domain registration, which cannot be undone.

amountCents.description: USD cents to add. Minimum 1000 ($10.00); presets are 1000, 2500, 5000, 10000. `amount_cents` is accepted as an alias.

country.description: Customer-declared ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 billing or residence country. Not nationality or IP.

countryPolicyVersion.description: Exact version read from GET /api/v1/billing/countries after presenting its restrictions to the customer.

WalletTopupRequest.description: New purchases require the full country declaration. Omitting all three declaration fields replays only an exact pre-country claim: checkout retains its original actor/kind/plan/credits fingerprint, and wallet retains its original amountCents fingerprint under the authenticated tenant and key. Missing claims fail country admission before insertion or provider I/O. Supplying any declaration never matches a legacy fingerprint. Retain the exact original countryPolicyVersion on retries; never substitute the current version.

url.description: Stripe Checkout URL to complete the top-up.

DomainRenewal.description: Renewal tracking for a domain purchased through Mailery. Null for a domain you connected yourself, which you renew where you bought it.

expires_at.description: Authoritative expiry for the registration, refreshed from the domain's registration record rather than assumed from the purchase date.

auto_renew.description: Customer opt-in. Auto-renew proceeds only when the prepaid wallet covers the quote; otherwise it notifies and leaves the domain alone.

registration_status.description: Registration state reported for the domain at its last refresh.

notices_sent.description: Lead-time notices already sent, keyed by threshold days (60/30/7).

autoRenew.description: Also set the auto-renew opt-in, applied only after the renewal charge succeeds.

wallet_debit_cents.description: Wallet cents debited before the renewal was submitted.

DomainWarmupStatus.description: Per-domain UTC-day recipient cap. Reservations include ambiguous attempts; this is not a delivered-mail count. Advances only on complete clean-day evidence. Capacity and pauses survive claim/account deletion for 30 days; feedback rates describe the current claim only.

InboundUsage.description: UTC monthly successfully imported recipient mailbox copies. Free 6000, Pro 20000, Scale 200000; one usage credit per overage copy. Test mail is unmetered. Near allowance starts at 80%; exhausted unfunded or suspended imports pause for bounded retry.

url.description: Relative URL rendering the immutable legal document with current shared footer chrome. Version hashes archived legal source, not presentation chrome.

checked.description: Ordinary candidate rows actually reclassified, bounded at 1000.

complete.description: All ordinary candidates and returned anomalies were covered; false forces ok false.

withdrawal_period.description: Unknown statutory eligibility remains review_required. No expired inference from local creation or fulfillment timestamps.

refund_policy_version.description: Exact purchase-time policy hash, or null when not established. No request-time substitution.

Forbidden.description: Token lacks the required scope or session type

RateLimited.description: Request was rate limited; Retry-After may be present

BillingRequired.description: Paid-surface gate (the custom-domain routes): the tenant needs an active subscription or a positive credit balance backed by a qualifying grant (details.required is active_subscription_or_credits; details.hint names the upgrade command). The free-tier surface — key minting, the shared-domain mailbox, metered sending, message operations — never returns this for a verified tenant. When the newest subscription is past_due, details.past_due_recovery names the two recovery paths: fix_payment via POST /api/v1/billing/portal, or spend_credits (cancel the subscription in the portal and keep spending the remaining qualifying credit balance).

SubscriptionExists.description: Tenant already has an active, trialing, or past_due subscription; manage it through POST /api/v1/billing/portal instead of subscribing again

WalletFundsRequired.description: The prepaid wallet does not cover this charge. `details` carries balance_cents, required_cents, shortfall_cents, suggested_topup_cents and a hint naming the add-funds command. Fails closed: the purchase or renewal is never submitted and nothing is charged.

get.summary: Health, deploy metadata, and a short-deadline DB ping

503.description: Degraded; the database ping failed or timed out

200.description: Markdown changelog of API contract changes

201.description: Session and account context. No API key secret is returned.

428.description: Explicit Terms acceptance missing or invalid

409.description: Account already exists or Terms version changed

503.description: Signup and new purchases are temporarily paused. Please try again later. Returned before any signup write for both legacy and explicit-consent callers when Terms publication is held.

400.description: Partial or invalid technical client declaration. Both headers must be valid or both omitted. Held publication returns 503 before declaration validation.

parameters.name: X-Mailery-Client-Name
parameters.description: Declared technical client name; supply together with version or omit both. No inference of human reading. Leading and trailing whitespace are invalid.

parameters.name: X-Mailery-Client-Version
parameters.description: Declared technical version; supply together with name or omit both. Leading and trailing whitespace are invalid.

post.description: Per-IP rate limit plus per-account exponential lockout: repeated failed logins against one email return 429 account_locked with a Retry-After header regardless of source IP. The lockout clears on successful login or password reset.

429.description: Rate limited or account locked (account_locked) with a Retry-After header

post.description: Uniform 200 whether or not an account exists for the email (no enumeration). The 200 is returned immediately: token issuance and email delivery run asynchronously after the response (failures are logged server-side, never surfaced), so neither the body nor response timing distinguishes real accounts from unknown emails. Rate-limited per IP and per email. Real accounts receive a single-use reset link that expires after 30 minutes; only a SHA-256 hash of the token is stored.

200.description: Accepted. The response is identical whether or not the account exists.

429.description: Rate limited (per IP or per email)

post.summary: Set a new password from a reset token
post.description: Consumes a single-use reset token, enforces the signup password policy, revokes every live session for the account, and clears any login lockout.

200.description: Password updated; all of the user's sessions are revoked

400.description: Invalid, expired, or already-used token (invalid_token) or password policy violation (bad_request)

post.summary: Verify an email address from a verification token
post.description: Consumes a single-use verification token (24-hour expiry) and marks the user's email verified.

400.description: Invalid, expired, or already-used token (invalid_token)

post.description: Requires an interactive user session. Rate-limited per user and per IP. Returns verified: true without sending when the email is already verified.

200.description: Verification email sent, or already verified

post.summary: Poll email-verification status for machine bootstrap (optionally mints a session)
post.description: Answers {"status":"pending"} until the emailed one-time verification link has been clicked. A caller presenting a live session token (Authorization: Bearer) for the SAME account receives {"status":"verified","token"} with a fresh session JWT carrying the normal login scope set once verification landed. Without that matching session the answer is always pending: unknown emails, unverified accounts, and verified accounts are indistinguishable (no enumeration), and email knowledge alone never mints a credential. Rate-limited hard per client IP (5/min) with a global ceiling; poll at >= 15s intervals.

email.description: The signup address; matched case-insensitively after trimming, exactly like signup.

400.description: Missing or non-string email (bad_request)

200.description: Provider flags and capabilities (password_reset, email_verification, email_verification_required)

get.summary: Export all tenant data as JSON (GDPR Art. 20). Owner/admin user session required; never billing-gated.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Messages and warm-up feedback receipts per independently paginated collection, 1-1000 (default200). Other collections are complete on each page.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Message id from a prior messages.next_cursor. Anything else is 400.

parameters.name: warmup_receipt_cursor
parameters.description: Receipt id from a prior domain_warmup_receipts.next_cursor; independent of the message cursor. Invalid UUID returns400.

parameters.name: withdrawal_cursor
parameters.description: Independent UUID cursor from withdrawal_evidence.next_cursor. Continue to null.

400.description: Invalid cursor

429.description: Export rate limited (600 requests per tenant per hour); resume from the same cursor in the next window

delete.summary: Permanently delete the account and all tenant data (GDPR Art. 17). Owner session + password re-auth required.

200.description: Tenant deleted; all sessions and API keys are revoked, every tenant-owned row is removed via cascade, and object storage-stored attachment binaries are removed best-effort after the cascade commits. An account.delete audit row survives with the tenant reference severed.

400.description: Password missing from the body

403.description: Password re-authentication failed, or the session is not the workspace owner

409.description: A non-canceled subscription exists (the check re-runs inside the deleting transaction, so a concurrently created subscription also aborts the delete); cancel it in the Stripe customer portal (POST /api/v1/billing/portal) first. Details list the blocking subscriptions.

post.description: Requires an interactive owner/admin user session. When MAILERY_REQUIRE_EMAIL_VERIFICATION is enabled (default in production), the verified-email requirement is enforced directly at this route, so a key can only be minted by a verified owner/admin session (403 email_verification_required otherwise). Available on the Free plan (PIVOT D-4): a verified tenant mints keys without any subscription or credit balance.

scopes.description: Omit for the least-privilege default ['mail_read','mail_write']. 'domains:purchase' must be requested explicitly.

201.description: One-time API key secret and record

post.description: Kill-switch that revokes every live API key for the tenant. Authenticates itself so it works with zero usable keys: send a valid session bearer token, OR send { email, password } in the body. The password path shares the per-account login lockout and is rate-limited per IP. Returns { ok, revoked, via }.

email.description: Required when not using a session bearer token.

password.description: Required when not using a session bearer token.

get.description: Returns the authenticated tenant actor's own feedback, newest first. Tenant-scoped and narrowed to the requesting actor. Not billing-gated.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Page size 1-200 (default 50).

post.description: Persists tenant-scoped product feedback via the @hasna/feedback SDK store. Any authenticated tenant actor (user session or API key) may submit — deliberately NOT billing-gated. Rate-limited to 30 per tenant and 60 per client IP per hour. post.summary: Send hosted mail from an outbound-ready tenant domain or the shared subdomain
post.description: Sends from a tenant-owned domain require the full domain-readiness gates and spend credits. Sends from the shared subdomain (MAILERY_SHARED_DOMAIN) skip the per-tenant domain gates; free-plan tenants are metered against the plan's monthly allowance (3,000 sends per UTC calendar month, no rollover), then any purchased credit balance. The message is assembled as raw RFC 5322 MIME and dispatched through the provider's raw content path, which is what carries attachments, In-Reply-To/References threading and a server-generated Message-Id on the sending domain (never caller-supplied: it is the identity a reply threads back to). Gate order, unchanged by the raw-MIME path: tenant suspension, request validation (recipients, attachments, headers, threading), mailbox ownership, shared-domain reputation kill-switch, sender-domain readiness, recipient suppression, referenced-attachment resolution, MIME assembly, metering, message row, dispatch. Status honesty: in live mode the message is persisted as queued and flips to sent only after SES accepted the dispatch (provider_message_id carries the SES id); on a server with MAILERY_MAIL_MODE != live no dispatch runs — the send is recorded with status test_sent, sent_at stays null, provider_message_id is null, and nothing is metered.

202.description: Accepted message. Live mode: status sent after the SES dispatch (queued is the pre-dispatch state). Non-live mode: status test_sent — recorded, not dispatched; provider_message_id is null. With an Idempotency-Key the body also carries `replayed` and `idempotency_key`.

400.description: bad_request (no valid recipient, malformed attachment list, non-base64 attachment content, both content and attachmentId on one attachment, a header value that is not a string or is over 900 characters, more than 10 headers or attachments) / header_not_allowed (a header name outside the allowlist) / idempotency_key_invalid

402.description: send_limit_reached (free monthly allowance and credit balance exhausted; details.hint names the upgrade command) or insufficient_credits (paid plan with a drained balance)

403.description: forbidden (the token lacks the required scope or session type) or tenant_suspended (the account is on a spend hold and cannot send). Both are checked BEFORE the meter is drawn, so nothing is charged.

404.description: not_found: the mailbox is not an active mailbox of this tenant, or a referenced attachmentId does not belong to it

409.description: Sender domain is missing ownership, DNS, outbound, enablement, billing, or restriction gates (sender_domain_not_ready / sender_domain_not_configured); recipient_suppressed; idempotency_key_conflict; idempotency_request_in_progress; send_outcome_ambiguous

413.description: payload_too_large: attachments exceed 10 MiB decoded in total, or the assembled raw message exceeds 15 MiB

503.description: send_state_write_failed: delivery status could not be recorded; error details contain message_id and send_outcome. A provider-dispatched attempt remains charged. Reuse its original idempotency key and reconcile the reference.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: YOUR stable key for this send (8-200 characters), optional. A repeated key with the same body replays the original response — marked `replayed: true` and echoed in the `Idempotent-Replay` response header — instead of sending, and metering, a second email; the same key with a different body is 409 idempotency_key_conflict. The FIRST terminal outcome (success or failure) is bound to the key, so a genuine retry after a terminal failure needs a fresh key. Callers supply their own key: no Mailery layer (server, SDK, CLI or MCP) ever invents one, because a key invented per attempt protects nothing and one invented per process would collapse two different sends into one. `idempotencyKey` in the body is accepted for transports that cannot set headers; the header wins.

post.summary: Send up to 100 hosted messages in one call
post.description: Each message takes the same body as POST /messages/send, may carry its own idempotencyKey, and gets its own result; one message's failure never aborts the batch. Every gate a single send passes runs for every message, in the same order. Metering: the meter is drawn ONCE, up front, in one transaction, for every message in the batch — all-or-nothing, so an unaffordable batch is one clean 402 send_limit_reached / insufficient_credits before anything is sent. Afterwards the units of messages that never reached the provider are returned: a message that failed strictly BEFORE its dispatch, and a message that replayed an earlier idempotency result (that original send drew and kept its own unit). A message that failed AFTER its dispatch KEEPS its unit — the provider may have accepted it — and its row records sendOutcome "ambiguous", exactly as a single send does. If the batch itself fails with an infrastructure error, nothing is refunded: how many messages reached the provider is unknown, and the safe side of that is over-charging, not free sends. Rate limit: the published per-tenant send limit (MAILERY_SEND_RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE, 60/min) counts ONE UNIT PER MESSAGE, so batching is not a way around the throttle that protects shared sending reputation. A batch that does not fit the remaining window is refused with 429 before anything is metered or sent — which also means the effective maximum batch is min(100, the remaining per-minute allowance). Requires mail_write; available on the Free plan. If status bookkeeping fails, send_state_write_failed carries message_id and send_outcome (ambiguous or not_dispatched). A provider-dispatched attempt retains its unit even if its stored row still looks queued; reuse the original idempotency key and reconcile the message reference.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Optional key for the WHOLE batch, in addition to the per-message keys. A repeated key replays the whole batch result rather than re-running it. Caller-supplied; never invented by Mailery.

200.description: Batch accepted and run. Per-message outcomes are in `results`; `metering` states what was drawn, kept and returned. A batch where every message failed is still a 200 — read `failed` and the per-message errors.

400.description: bad_request (messages is missing, empty, carries more than 100 entries, or an entry is not an object — the message names the index) / idempotency_key_invalid (a per-item key outside 8-200 characters, the message names the index). Every one of these is raised BEFORE the meter is drawn, so the batch is metered not at all and sends nothing.

402.description: send_limit_reached / insufficient_credits: the tenant cannot pay for the whole batch. Nothing was sent and nothing was metered.

403.description: forbidden (the token lacks the required scope or session type) or tenant_suspended (the account is on a spend hold and cannot send). Both are checked BEFORE the meter is drawn, so nothing is charged.

503.description: batch_refund_failed: per-message outcomes are recorded but refund settlement failed. Error details include batch_id, unit, refundable and metered_at for operator reconciliation; no successful refund is claimed.

post.summary: Add funds to the prepaid wallet
post.description: First paid opening: new wallet funding is disabled (409 wallet_funding_disabled). Existing exact-key replay and observation-only reconciliation remain available. Opens a one-time Stripe Checkout Session that credits the wallet on `checkout.session.completed`. Owner session and a verified email are required, the same 10/hour limit as POST /api/v1/billing/checkout applies, and an Idempotency-Key header is REQUIRED so a retry replays the same session instead of opening a second payable one. Lost provider results, local persistence failures or unresolved success bookkeeping return checkout_outcome_ambiguous: keep the original key and reconcile that attempt before another purchase. An expired claim lease cannot start another session. First read GET /api/v1/billing/countries and present the list before payment. Requires country, countryBasis (billing or residence), and countryPolicyVersion. Listed countries are refused before provider I/O. The declaration is bound to the authenticated actor and purchase fingerprint and copied to Stripe metadata. Stripe billing-address editing is not locked or independently verified.  New purchases require the full country declaration. Omitting all three declaration fields replays only an exact pre-country claim: checkout retains its original actor/kind/plan/credits fingerprint, and wallet retains its original amountCents fingerprint under the authenticated tenant and key. Missing claims fail country admission before insertion or provider I/O. Supplying any declaration never matches a legacy fingerprint. Retain the exact original countryPolicyVersion on retries; never substitute the current version. Exact pre-country wallet replay projects only the historical terminal status409 request_outcome_ambiguous error to checkout_outcome_ambiguous with same-key reconciliation advice. Stored claim bytes and every unrelated terminal outcome remain unchanged.

400.description: Amount below the $10 minimum, above the maximum, or a missing/invalid Idempotency-Key; checkout_country_required, checkout_country_invalid, or checkout_country_basis_required

503.description: Billing is not configured on this server

428.description: A new paid-entry admission requires tenant owner acceptance of the exact current Terms. Idempotent replays and reconciliation retain their original admission.

409.description: checkout_outcome_ambiguous for an unresolved payable attempt, idempotency_request_in_progress, checkout_country_policy_changed or idempotency_key_conflict. Retain the original purchase key and reconcile it before starting another purchase. First paid opening: new wallet funding is disabled (409 wallet_funding_disabled).

post.summary: Renew a Mailery-registered domain, charged to the prepaid wallet
post.description: First paid opening: new purchases and renewals are disabled (409 domain_sales_disabled); setup without buy/purchase remains available. Existing exact-key replay and observation-only reconciliation remain available. Debits the exact all-in renewal quote from the prepaid wallet in the same transaction that claims the renewal, BEFORE the renewal is submitted. An insufficient balance returns 402 with the shortfall and nothing is submitted or charged. Requires the domains:purchase scope and an Idempotency-Key header.

400.description: Missing or invalid Idempotency-Key

409.description: The domain was not purchased through Mailery, its expiry could not be confirmed, the renewal was refused upstream (nothing charged), or the outcome is ambiguous and awaits reconciliation First paid opening: new purchases and renewals are disabled (409 domain_sales_disabled); setup without buy/purchase remains available.

428.description: A new paid-entry admission requires tenant owner acceptance of the exact current Terms. Idempotent replays and reconciliation retain their original admission.

post.summary: Set the auto-renew opt-in for a Mailery-registered domain
post.description: First paid opening: enabling automatic renewal returns 409 domain_sales_disabled; disabling remains available. Auto-renew is OFF by default. When on, the renewal poller renews the domain only if the prepaid wallet covers the quote; otherwise it emits a domain.expiring notice with the shortfall and leaves the domain alone. Charges nothing, so no Idempotency-Key is required.

400.description: enabled must be a boolean

409.description: domain_sales_disabled when enabling automatic renewal while domain sales are closed
